sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in C.T. Case No.37 of 2021 pending on the file of learned Addl.
Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Phulbani, arising out Belghar P.S. Case No.16 of 2021 for commission of the offence under Sections 376(2)(n)/506 IPC and Section 6 of the POSCO Act.
3. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s. 439 Cr.P.C by the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Phulbani, by order dated 13.12.2022 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner, who is the first offender, is in custody since 13.06.2021 and in the meanwhile the victim including her parents and other material witnesses have been examined.
Hence, he may be released on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail during currency of trial.

6. Taking into account the statement of the victim P.W.3 and the evidence of the doctor, P.W. 7, this Court directs the Petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned court in seisin.

7. Additionally, it is directed that the Petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station Hemant Patra vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167196165/
1 once every week on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.

sentences.text: Certification of such appearance shall be submitted to the Court in seisin.
The Petitioner shall not threaten the Informant and/or his family members.
It shall be open to the Informant/Prosecution to seek variance of this order in the event there is any threat perception.
8. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
9. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
